itens.t: Seoul shares soar over 4 percent to snap three-day slide on tech rally
itens.r: South Korean stocks finished more than 4 percent higher on Tuesday to snap three consecutive sessions of sharp decline. The rebound was driven by strong gains in technology shares. Meanwhile, oil prices dropped sharply on global economic hopes. Currency markets also reflected the shift as the South Korean won climbed against the U.S. dollar.
itens.d:
South Korean stocks finished more than 4 percent higher on Tuesday to snap three consecutive sessions of sharp decline. The rebound was driven by strong gains in technology shares, while oil prices dropped sharply on hopes for the possible end of the war in the Middle East.

The benchmark Korea Composite Stock Price Index closed up 220.28 points, or 4.39 percent, to reach 5,239.13 after rising as high as 5,300.92 during the session. Following a strong opening, the Korea Exchange activated a buy-side sidecar for the main bourse.
itens.e:
South Korean stocks experienced a sharp rebound on Tuesday, soaring more than 4 percent to snap a three-day losing streak. The market recovery was propelled by strong gains in technology shares and a steep drop in oil prices, the latter occurring amid rising hopes for a potential end to the conflict in the Middle East. The benchmark Korea Composite Stock Price Index gained 220.28 points to close at 5,239.13, after reaching as high as 5,300.92 during a session that also prompted the activation of a buy-side sidecar by the Korea Exchange.

This dramatic surge matters deeply to domestic investors and market participants who weathered three consecutive sessions of steep declines earlier in the week. The interplay between local tech equity valuations and external commodity pressures, particularly oil, highlights how swiftly regional financial sentiment can shift in response to overseas geopolitical developments. The activation of the trading sidecar underscores the sheer volatility currently characterizing the main bourse.

One risk is whether the optimism surrounding oil prices and Middle East hostilities will prove durable enough to sustain the index near these elevated levels. Observers will watch closely to see if technology shares maintain their upward momentum or if external macroeconomic headwinds quickly reassert themselves over the coming trading sessions.

itens.t: North Korea says navy to deploy new high-speed torpedo in early 2027
itens.r: North Korea tested a new-type high-speed torpedo weapon system on Monday, marking the second public test of the weapon in the last month. State media reported that the navy is scheduled to deploy the system in early 2027.
itens.d:
North Korea tested a new-type high-speed torpedo weapon system on Monday, marking the second public test of the weapon within the last month. State media reported the event following observations by the Korean Central News Agency.

According to the state reports released on Tuesday, the new-type torpedo weapon system is scheduled to be equipped by the country's navy starting from the beginning of 2027.
itens.e:
North Korea conducted a public test of a new-type high-speed torpedo weapon system on Monday, marking its second test of the weapon within a single month. State media reported the event, observed by the Korean Central News Agency, and announced that the naval armament is scheduled for official deployment to the country's naval forces beginning in early 2027.

This development matters for regional security dynamics on the Korean Peninsula, directly affecting military readiness and threat perceptions among neighboring nations. The formal timeline indicating a 2027 fleet introduction suggests a methodical progression from testing phases to active operational capability, signaling sustained defense modernization efforts by Pyongyang.

One risk is that continued weapons testing could further entrench regional distrust and escalate security dilemmas. Observers will watch for subsequent state media announcements regarding potential additional tests or further details concerning the operational capabilities of the new naval system ahead of its scheduled deployment.

itens.t: North Korea accuses UN chief of favoring South Korea after DMZ blast
itens.r: North Korea expressed regret over comments by the United Nations secretary-general, who urged both Koreas to reduce tensions through dialogue following a recent explosion. Pyongyang accused the UN chief of taking a prejudiced attitude.
itens.d:
North Korea expressed regret over comments made by UN Secretary-General António Guterres, who urged both Koreas to reduce tensions through dialogue following a landmine explosion at the border. State media accused the UN chief of taking Seoul's side.

Kim Yo Jong, an influential sister of North Korean leader Kim Jong Un, called Guterres's posture prejudiced and irresponsible for reproducing South Korea's unilateral version of the September explosion in the Demilitarized Zone that seriously injured several South Korean soldiers.
itens.e:
North Korea issued a sharp diplomatic rebuke against UN Secretary-General António Guterres following his calls for both Koreas to reduce tensions through dialogue. The UN chief's appeal followed a landmine explosion inside the Demilitarized Zone that seriously injured several South Korean soldiers. State media and Kim Yo Jong, the influential sister of leader Kim Jong Un, accused Guterres of maintaining a prejudiced and irresponsible posture by allegedly reproducing South Korea's unilateral version of the September border incident.

This diplomatic friction matters because it underscores the deep divide at the United Nations level regarding accountability for border escalations on the peninsula. The direct criticism from Pyongyang affects the perceived impartiality of international mediators attempting to broker dialogue between the two nations.

One risk is that deepening friction between Pyongyang and the UN leadership could further diminish prospects for constructive cross-border communication. Observers will watch to see if the diplomatic sparring leads to further escalation or alters the international community's approach to monitoring security incidents along the Demilitarized Zone.

itens.t: Work on southern section of inter-Korean railway to resume soon, says Seoul
itens.r: South Korea's Vice Unification Minister announced that construction will soon resume on the South Korean section of a railway line meant to link the two Koreas. The remarks came during a policy seminar in Seoul.
itens.d:
South Korea will soon resume construction on the southern section of a railway line meant to link the two Koreas, according to Vice Unification Minister Kim Nam-jung. The remarks were made during a seminar in Seoul as the government seeks to restore the Gyeongwon Line.

The planned restoration work aims to prepare a path connecting the two Koreas between Baekmagoji and Woljeong-ri Station, close to the Demilitarized Zone. Restoration initially began in 2015 but was stopped in May 2016 following actions by North Korea.

itens.t: NASA unveils $10 billion in moon base contracts and nuclear rover plan
itens.r: NASA is pushing ahead with its plan to build a permanent lunar base for astronauts by 2032. The agency unveiled up to $10 billion in contracts to deliver cargo to the moon and develop a nuclear-powered rover.
itens.d:
NASA is pushing ahead with its plan to build a moon base for astronauts by 2032, unveiling up to $10 billion in contracts to launch and deliver cargo. The announcement was made during the agency's Max Power air show event at the Kennedy Space Center.

The initiative includes a new $10 billion Commercial Lunar Payload Services framework dubbed CLPS 2, funding for the Venture-Class Acquisition of Dedicated and Rideshare program, and the nuclear-powered PROMISE rover. NASA selected eight companies to compete for the new missions.

itens.t: SpaceX targets Nov. 13 for epic double-catch Starship Flight 15 test
itens.r: SpaceX announced it is targeting Friday, Nov. 13, for the 15th test flight of its Starship megarocket. The ambitious mission will feature another attempt at the company's signature booster catch.
itens.d:
SpaceX is targeting Friday, November 13, for the 15th test flight of its Starship megarocket, which will attempt an unprecedented double-catch maneuver. Both the Super Heavy booster and the Starship upper-stage spacecraft are planned to return to the launch site.

If successful, this will mark the first full recovery of an orbital launch system using the tower's chopstick arms at Starbase in South Texas. While Super Heavy has been caught previously, Ship has never attempted the maneuver.

itens.t: Are Webb telescope's 'Little Red Dots' tiny black holes from Big Bang?
itens.r: NASA's James Webb Space Telescope continues to puzzle astronomers with its observations of the early universe. Researchers are investigating whether mysterious 'Little Red Dots' are ancient black holes.
itens.d:
New research suggests that the James Webb Space Telescope's mysterious Little Red Dots might be connected to primordial black holes. These tiny objects would have been born from fluctuations in matter density just after the Big Bang, predating stars and galaxies.

Researchers tested whether a Little Red Dot known as Abell 2744-QSO1 could host a primordial black hole. Unlike black holes born from stellar deaths, these objects originate from the exponential expansion of the early universe.

itens.t: What the Nvidia crisis teaches about the era of rockstar CEOs
itens.r: Jensen Huang has transformed Nvidia into a global tech titan, but recent market volatility highlights the risks of corporate dependence on single visionary leaders. Analysts point to the immense pressure facing the semiconductor sector.
itens.d:
Jensen Huang is the architect of Nvidia's rise to a multi-trillion-dollar giant at the center of the artificial intelligence boom. However, the CEO recently found himself at the center of a scandal after admitting to a relationship with an executive reported to have worked with Chinese intelligence.

This controversy highlights the key-man risk across the technology sector, where the fortunes of powerful companies are closely tied to individual leaders. Similar dependencies exist around prominent CEOs like Elon Musk, Sam Altman, and Mark Zuckerberg.

The administration is reportedly attempting to advance key agendas during this transition while hoping for favorable decisions from the Supreme Federal Tribunal to improve dialogue with the legislature.

itens.t: Supreme Court closure of long-running fake news inquiry sparks debate
itens.r: The president of Brazil's Supreme Federal Court formally closed the high-profile fake news investigation overseen by Justice Alexandre de Moraes. Legal experts note that broader related investigations remain active.
itens.d:
The President of Brazil's Supreme Federal Tribunal, Edson Fachin, archived a long-running fake news inquiry that had been conducted for over seven years. However, the decision does not immediately dismiss all related investigations.

Fachin determined that 104 individual procedures linked to the main inquiry must be examined separately to decide whether to continue, archive, or transfer them. Previous evidence and judicial decisions remain valid.

itens.t: Brazil Supreme Court holds conciliation hearing on 6x1 work scale
itens.r: Brazil's Supreme Federal Court hosted a special conciliation hearing to address the proposed reduction of the traditional 6x1 work schedule. Labor representatives and lawmakers debated the economic impacts.
itens.d:
Brazil's Supreme Federal Tribunal scheduled a conciliation hearing to discuss the implementation of ending the 6x1 work scale. The meeting brings together business representatives, industry leaders, workers, and government officials ahead of new constitutional rules.

The new regulations will gradually reduce the maximum weekly work hours from 44 to 40 hours without salary reductions. The transition involves a first step lowering the limit to 42 hours with two rest days per week.

Cristiano Ronaldo announced his exit from the national squad in early November following a relationship crisis with coach Jorge Jesus over playing time. Despite his departure, the team secured subsequent victories in the UEFA Nations League.

itens.t: One in four adolescents globally lacks physical activity, WHO study finds
itens.r: A comprehensive international study published by the World Health Organization reveals that a significant portion of teenagers fail to meet minimum exercise guidelines. Researchers warn of long-term public health consequences.
itens.d:
A study released by the World Health Organization reveals that one in four adolescents globally lacks sufficient physical activity. This affects approximately 240 million young people aged 11 to 17 who fail to exercise for 60 minutes daily.

Physical inactivity serves as a major risk factor for heart disease, type 2 diabetes, and certain cancers. Health experts emphasize that regular exercise helps reduce obesity and improves overall physical and mental health.

itens.d:

Writing in his column, Matthäus noted that the club willingly agreed to Musiala's contract terms and salary. He compared the situation to teammate Michael Olise to emphasize that contracts should be respected regardless of performance fluctuations.
